validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own wiki page for P0784 sources its three key numbers from three DIFFERENT, mostly off-topic citations, and none of the three actually describes a single distinct pipeline matching this row's name. Per the gem.wiki infobox/citation trail: Length=164km is sourced to ngpedia.ru (a page about the Shebelinka gas FIELD, not a route-length source); Diameter=1200mm is sourced to a prozorro.gov.ua procurement TENDER for the TSO corporate entity (a generic company-registration record, not a pipeline spec sheet); Capacity=24 bcm/y is sourced to Gainutdinova (2012), an academic article about Arctic/regional gas-market formation. I fetched the Gainutdinova article directly (cyberleninka.ru, verified live, independent of GEM) and it does NOT support a standalone 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail' pipeline at all: its export-capacity-at-western-border table has ONE combined row reading 'Ананьев - тирасполь - Измаил, Шебелинка - Измаил (три нитки) 24' (Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail, Shebelinka-Izmail (three threads) = 24 bcm/y to Romania/Bulgaria/Greece/Turkey/Macedonia) -- i.e. 24 bcm/y is an AGGREGATE figure spanning BOTH the Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail line (already tracked separately as P0786, itself 1200mm/23.7 bcm/y per its own GEM page citing KPMG 2017 -- essentially the whole 24 bcm/y already) AND a 'Shebelinka-Izmail (three threads)' system, not a capacity belonging to one pipeline named 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail'. Cross-checked against Ukrainian Wikipedia's 'Shebelinka-Izmail gas transport corridor' article (uk.wikipedia.org, verified live, independent secondary source citing Moldovatransgaz's own company history and a Moldovan government gasification-program document): the corridor's real named pipelines are (a) Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Odesa/-Odesa-2 (ШДО/ШДО-2), (b) Roздільна-Izmail, 820mm, commissioned Oct 1973 -- this is P0787, and (c) Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail (шдкрі, 'SHDKRI'), commissioned 1975 with TWO threads of 800mm each -- together SHDKRI + Rozdilna-Izmail could supply UP TO 15.8 bcm/y combined to the Balkans (per the cited Moldovan document), a figure that matches neither GEM's 24 bcm/y nor P0787's own 7.3 bcm/y. GEM's P0784 row name is a garbled fusion of the real SHDKRI route ('Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih') with the endpoint of the SEPARATE Rozdilna-Izmail line ('Rozdilna-Izmail') tacked on -- a name that does not correspond to any single pipeline in the sourced history. Its diameter (1200mm) and capacity (24 bcm/y) instead match P0786 (Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail, 1200mm/23.7 bcm/y) almost exactly, not SHDKRI's real 800mm/partial-15.8bcm/y or Rozdilna-Izmail's real 820mm. Most likely explanation: whoever built this GEM row read the Gainutdinova (2012) combined-corridor table row, split its two comma-separated route labels into two GEM entities, and (mis)assigned the SAME diameter/capacity pulled from Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail's own sourcing to the second (Shebelinka-Izmail) label, then invented a composite name blending SHDKRI with Rozdilna-Izmail. Two independent, non-GEM sources (Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article + the Gainutdinova 2012 academic article) corroborate this reconstruction; tier medium (both are secondary/tertiary, no single primary per-pipeline TSO document was found for SHDKRI specifically). This is NOT a claim that no real pipeline exists along the Shebelinka-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail route -- SHDKRI is real and built 1975 -- but P0784 AS RECORDED (this name + these specs) does not correspond to it, to Rozdilna-Izmail, or to Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail individually; it reads as a data-entry artifact straddling all three.

validity.recommendation: Do not patch Length/Diameter/Capacity individually -- they are downstream symptoms of the duplicate/composite-entity issue above and should be corrected (or the row retired/merged) only as part of the cluster adjudication.
validity.researcher_notes: All three headline specs fail independent corroboration for THIS specific route: (1) Length=164km -- geographically implausible on its own terms: the named route runs Shebelinka (Kharkiv Oblast) via Dnipropetrovsk and Kryvyi Rih to Izmail (Odesa Oblast, Romanian border), a corridor whose real sub-segments alone exceed 164km (Rozdilna-Izmail alone is already tracked at 230km as P0787; Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk alone was 197.5km per Ukrainian Wikipedia's sourced history). 164km would not even cover the shortest named leg. It is plausible (not confirmed) that 164km is actually the Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih road/pipe distance mistakenly applied as the whole pipeline's length, but I found no source stating this explicitly -- flagging rather than asserting. (2) Diameter=1200mm does not match SHDKRI's sourced 800mm (x2 threads) or Rozdilna-Izmail's sourced 820mm; it matches Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail's (P0786) 1200mm instead. (3) Capacity=24 bcm/y is an aggregate multi-corridor figure per the Gainutdinova (2012) source table (see duplicate finding above), not a single-pipeline capacity; the real SHDKRI+Rozdilna-Izmail combined figure documented elsewhere is 15.8 bcm/y, and SHDKRI alone (2x800mm threads) would be a fraction of that. No independent source was found that states 164km/1200mm/24bcm/y together as the profile of one distinct, named Ukrainian gas pipeline.

validity.recommendation: No change to Status/Fuel/StartLocation/EndLocation or the state-operator Owner attribution; these are correct regardless of how the duplicate/spec concerns above are eventually resolved.
validity.researcher_notes: Independent of the entity-identity problem above, the row's coarse facts hold up: (a) Fuel=Gas and Status=operating are true of every real candidate this row could represent (SHDKRI, Rozdilna-Izmail, or the broader corridor) -- Ukraine's Shebelinka-Izmail gas transport system remains part of the operating GTS regardless of the 1 Jan 2025 end of RU-UA transit (per country-standing guidance, transit cessation alone is not evidence of retirement, and no line-specific evidence of decommissioning was found). (b) StartLocation=Shebelinka / EndLocation=Izmail match the real corridor's documented endpoints in Ukrainian Wikipedia's sourced history regardless of which internal segment P0784 is meant to represent. (c) Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' at 100% is correctly NOT Gazprom -- consistent with the country-standing rule that Ukraine's transmission assets have been in Ukrainian state hands since the Ukrtransgaz-to-GTSOU unbundling completed 1 Jan 2020 (confirmed independently via GTSOU's LinkedIn company page and UNIAN's contemporaneous reporting on the Naftogaz-MGU unbundling roadmap). Minor unresolved nuance (not P0784-specific, not proposed as a fix here): GTSOU (LLC) is technically the certified operating subsidiary of JSC Mahistralni Gazoprovody Ukrainy (MGU, 100% state-owned via the Ministry of Finance), which some sources describe as the asset-owning parent -- GEM's 'Owner1 = Gas TSO of Ukraine' may be a one-tier simplification of that two-tier state structure, applied uniformly across Ukraine gas rows on this tracker.

summary: P0784 flagged CONCERN (duplicate + spec): its name garbles two real, historically distinct pipelines (SHDKRI, 1975, 2x800mm / Rozdilna-Izmail, 1973, 820mm, already tracked as P0787) and its diameter/capacity (1200mm/24bcm/y) instead match a third, separately-tracked pipeline (P0786 Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail, 1200mm/23.7bcm/y) via a mis-derived aggregate figure in the sheet's own cited source (Gainutdinova 2012); Length=164km is geographically implausible for this route.
